newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: White right sees rand fall as verdict on S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: White right sees rand fall as verdict on S.Africa.

text.p: Right-wing fringe groups on Wednesday described the plunge in South Africa's rand currency as evidence that the rest of the world shared their mistrust of the black government.
"For investors, there are clear signs that lasting peace and progress are not possible in the present unitary state," the Conservative Party (CP) said in a statement.
"It is for this reason that trust in the country is collapsing and that the rand has reached its lowest level ever."
The rand, which stood at about 3.70 to the dollar in February, has steadily fallen since then and was trading at 4.71 to the dollar on Wednesday.
The Afrikaner Resistance Movement (AWB) of Eugene Terre Blanche said in a separate statement that the currency was bound to fall further.
"Is it any wonder that investors don't want to invest here? Any investor who trusts this government with his money will have to watch his investment lose value," the AWB said.
"This country is falling into chaos so fast that it is impossible to keep up day by day with the corruption, scandals and thievery," it said.

The CP, which boycotted the 1994 election in which President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress swept to power, said the only option for white Afrikaners was to set up their own sovereign state where they could live according to their own standards and principles.
It said the ANC's inability to combat crime and corruption had caused a loss of confidence in South Africa.
